concepts.title: Activation functions
concepts.meaning: Adds a nonlinear transformation between affine neural-network layers.
concepts.brief: Build a small coordinate-plane SVG with selectable sigmoid, tanh, ReLU, and GELU curves; align each curve with its input and output values and mark saturation or the ReLU kink.
concepts.aliases: nonlinearity; sigmoid; tanh; ReLU; GELU
pitfalls: Curve shape is a local mathematical property, not a complete explanation of network behavior.
Show the actual axes and domain.

concepts.title: Autoregressive generation loop
concepts.meaning: Produces a sequence by selecting one next token conditioned on the prompt and prior generated tokens.
concepts.brief: Show prompt tokens entering prefill, last-position logits flowing through a sampler, one selected token appending to the stream, and KV state reused on the next decode step.
concepts.aliases: next-token loop; prefill; decode; token sampling
pitfalls: Future tokens are generated sequentially in this loop.
Sampling settings alter the distribution and do not guarantee answer quality.

concepts.title: Backpropagation graph
concepts.meaning: Moves derivatives backward through a computation graph and adds contributions where paths meet.
concepts.brief: Show a minimal forward DAG for two inputs sharing one intermediate value, place local derivatives on edges, then animate reverse adjoints and addition at the shared node.
concepts.aliases: computation graph; reverse-mode autodiff; chain rule
pitfalls: The reverse pass computes vector-Jacobian products; it does not materialize a full Jacobian.
Distinguish a local derivative from the accumulated gradient.

concepts.title: Bayesian update
concepts.meaning: Combines a prior distribution with observed-data likelihood to form a posterior distribution.
concepts.brief: Animate a Beta prior over success probability, a binomial likelihood from observed successes and trials, and the normalized posterior; expose how additional evidence narrows or shifts uncertainty.
concepts.aliases: prior; likelihood; posterior; posterior predictive
pitfalls: A posterior depends on the stated prior, data model, and sampling assumptions.
Do not depict a point estimate as the entire posterior.

concepts.title: Causal graph patterns
concepts.meaning: Uses directed graphs to encode assumptions about causal relationships and adjustment.
concepts.brief: Create three side-by-side causal motifs: chain, fork/confounder, and collider. Highlight which variables to condition on for each question and optionally distinguish observation from intervention with a separate do marker.
concepts.aliases: causal DAG; confounder; mediator; collider; intervention
pitfalls: A DAG encodes assumptions; observed correlation alone does not identify causal effects.
Conditioning on a collider can create an association.

concepts.title: Chat template and training data flow
concepts.meaning: Serializes conversational records into token streams and assigns loss to selected positions.
concepts.brief: Show structured role/content messages rendered into special tokens, tokenized, packed with boundaries, and paired with a loss mask that includes assistant targets while retaining prompt context.
concepts.aliases: chat template; assistant-only loss; packing; loss mask
pitfalls: Templates are tokenizer/model-specific serialization contracts.
Packed examples need attention isolation where required; loss masks and attention masks serve different jobs.

concepts.title: Classification confusion matrix
concepts.meaning: Counts predicted labels against true labels so each error type remains visible.
concepts.brief: Render an accessible 2×2 or multiclass grid with truth on rows and predictions on columns; animate one example into TP, FP, FN, or TN and keep denominators labeled.
concepts.aliases: true positive; false positive; false negative; true negative
pitfalls: Axis orientation differs across libraries; label both axes explicitly.
Accuracy alone hides class-specific error costs.

concepts.title: Compute-optimal training allocation
concepts.meaning: Shows how a fixed compute budget can be allocated across model size, data, and later inference costs.
concepts.brief: Render a compute budget slider that trades parameters against training tokens, then overlays loss/quality curves and serving-cost constraints; compare a training-only optimum with a lifetime-cost choice.
concepts.aliases: Chinchilla allocation; scaling laws; compute budget
pitfalls: Scaling-law fits are empirical within measured regimes and may not extrapolate across architectures or data regimes.
Keep training and lifetime inference costs separate.

concepts.title: Conformal prediction and coverage
concepts.meaning: Calibrates a prediction set or interval using held-out nonconformity scores and a finite-sample rank.
concepts.brief: Sort calibration errors, mark the finite-sample quantile rank, then apply the threshold to new predictions. Show interval width and empirical hits across a stream of exchangeable test points.
concepts.aliases: split conformal; prediction set; calibration quantile
pitfalls: The standard guarantee is marginal under exchangeability; it does not ensure exact conditional coverage in every subgroup.
Show the calibration/test split explicitly.

concepts.title: Convolution and receptive field
concepts.meaning: Applies a shared local filter across image positions and combines channels into feature maps.
concepts.brief: Slide a small weighted kernel over a grid, reveal each dot-product output, then stack layers and show how the effective receptive field grows. Let padding/stride alter output shape.
concepts.aliases: convolution kernel; feature map; receptive field; pooling
pitfalls: Padding adds boundary values and can create artificial edge evidence.
Keep filter weights and input values visible for worked examples.

concepts.title: Decision-tree split
concepts.meaning: Partitions feature space through sequential tests and assigns a prediction to each leaf.
concepts.brief: Use a tiny two-feature plane with one threshold boundary, then grow a second split and color leaves by class mix; optionally display weighted Gini or entropy reduction at the chosen split.
concepts.aliases: decision node; leaf; Gini gain; information gain
pitfalls: A tree split is an axis-aligned partition in the shown feature coordinates.
Impurity reduction is a training criterion, not held-out performance.

concepts.title: Distributed collective operations
concepts.meaning: Coordinates tensor movement or reduction across participating ranks.
concepts.brief: Draw ranks as lanes and animate all-reduce, reduce-scatter, all-gather, and all-to-all over a labeled ring or mesh; show payload and synchronization boundary.
concepts.aliases: all-reduce; all-gather; reduce-scatter; all-to-all
pitfalls: Rank order, topology, and collective implementation affect cost and correctness.
Do not depict collectives as free shared-memory operations.

concepts.title: Model drift and delayed labels
concepts.meaning: Separates input distribution changes from performance evidence that arrives after outcomes mature.
concepts.brief: Plot reference and live feature distributions with a separate timeline for predictions, label maturity, and score updates; distinguish data drift alerts from measured model error.
concepts.aliases: data drift; concept drift; label delay; monitoring
pitfalls: Input drift alone does not establish quality degradation.
Missing labels can be delayed, selectively observed, or unavailable.

concepts.title: Embedding neighborhood map
concepts.meaning: Shows how a similarity metric ranks nearby vectors in a learned representation space.
concepts.brief: Draw a labeled point cloud with a query vector, cosine-angle and Euclidean-distance rulers, nearest-neighbor highlights, and an optional PCA projection toggle; retain vector labels and metric readouts.
concepts.aliases: vector space; cosine similarity; nearest neighbors; PCA projection
pitfalls: A two-dimensional projection can distort global distances and hide task-relevant dimensions.
Equal vector dimensions do not prove compatible coordinate systems.

concepts.title: Floating-point formats
concepts.meaning: Represents signed values with finite exponent range and finite precision determined by a bit layout.
concepts.brief: Design a scalable bit-field SVG for sign, exponent, and fraction; pair it with neighboring representable numbers and range/precision comparisons for FP16, BF16, FP32, and FP8 variants.
concepts.aliases: FP16; BF16; FP8; exponent; mantissa; ULP
pitfalls: Range and precision are different properties.
Label the exact format and bias; bit allocations vary.

concepts.title: Tiled matrix multiplication
concepts.meaning: Reuses input tiles in fast local memory to reduce global-memory traffic during matrix multiplication.
concepts.brief: Animate small A and B tiles loaded from global memory into shared SRAM, multiply-accumulate into a register tile, then write output. Expose tile reuse, edge predicates, and accumulator precision.
concepts.aliases: GEMM tiling; shared memory; Tensor Core tile; matrix multiply
pitfalls: Tile shapes and supported arithmetic depend on hardware and kernel contracts.
Reduced-precision products may still use higher-precision accumulation.

concepts.title: GPU execution hierarchy
concepts.meaning: Maps host launches and memory ownership to GPU grids, blocks, threads, warps, and multiprocessors.
concepts.brief: Show a CPU host launching a grid of blocks; expand one block into warps/threads mapped onto an SM, with separate host and device-memory regions and synchronization points.
concepts.aliases: kernel launch; grid; block; warp; SM; device memory
pitfalls: Terminology and scheduling details vary by accelerator and architecture.
Use separate counts for logical threads and physical execution lanes.

concepts.title: Gradient descent landscape
concepts.meaning: Shows how a parameter update follows a local gradient on an objective surface.
concepts.brief: Render a 2D contour surface over two parameters with a live point, gradient arrow, and short sequence of proposed updates; allow learning-rate changes to reveal stable, slow, and overshooting paths.
concepts.aliases: loss surface; optimization path; step size
pitfalls: Convex bowls are teaching examples; many neural-network objectives are nonconvex.
The gradient arrow is local and depends on the displayed coordinates and scale.

concepts.title: Learning-rate schedule
concepts.meaning: Changes the optimizer step scale according to training progress.
concepts.brief: Draw a timeline with warmup followed by selectable constant, linear-decay, and cosine-decay curves; pair the curve with current step and scalar learning rate.
concepts.aliases: warmup; cosine decay; learning-rate curve
pitfalls: The schedule changes update scale, not the gradient direction.
Avoid implying one schedule is universally best.

concepts.title: Dynamic loss scaling controller
concepts.meaning: Scales a training loss to keep small gradients representable, then detects overflow before the optimizer update.
concepts.brief: Trace scale-up before backward, gradient unscale before clipping, finite-value check, optimizer-step skip on overflow, and scale backoff/growth across iterations.
concepts.aliases: GradScaler; overflow backoff; gradient underflow
pitfalls: Loss scaling changes numerical range during gradient computation; it does not improve model quality by itself.
Keep unscale and finite checks before the optimizer step.

concepts.title: Model parallelism topologies
concepts.meaning: Splits model computation or state across devices along different dimensions.
concepts.brief: Show the same transformer mapped as replicated data-parallel workers, tensor-parallel shards within a layer, pipeline stages across layers, context shards, and expert ownership. Use separate colors for communication edges.
concepts.aliases: tensor parallel; pipeline parallel; data parallel; context parallel; expert parallel
pitfalls: Parallelism modes shard different axes and introduce distinct communication patterns.
A combined topology has divisibility and placement constraints.

concepts.title: Optimizer state and moments
concepts.meaning: Maintains gradient history and coordinate scale to compute parameter updates.
concepts.brief: Show a parameter beside its gradient stream, momentum buffer m, squared-gradient buffer v, bias-corrected values, and the resulting update. Add a separate decoupled weight-decay arrow for AdamW.
concepts.aliases: momentum; Adam; AdamW; optimizer buffers
pitfalls: Adam second moment averages squared gradients and is not statistical variance.
Keep weight decay distinct from the adaptive-gradient term.

concepts.title: Preference-training pipeline
concepts.meaning: Turns comparisons between responses into a reward model or a direct preference-optimization objective.
concepts.brief: Show prompt plus chosen/rejected responses feeding a pairwise score difference, Bradley-Terry sigmoid/BCE, and reward-head update; optionally branch to PPO with a reference policy or DPO direct policy loss.
concepts.aliases: Bradley-Terry; reward model; RLHF; DPO; chosen/rejected pair
pitfalls: Human preference labels measure the annotation contract and can contain noise or bias.
Reward-model score is a learned proxy; keep held-out human evaluation visible.

concepts.title: Recurrent and gated state
concepts.meaning: Carries a learned state through an ordered sequence, with LSTM/GRU gates controlling updates.
concepts.brief: Unroll three sequence steps with shared weights; trace hidden state and, for LSTM, separate cell state through forget/input/output gates. Highlight how a distant gradient travels backward.
concepts.aliases: RNN; LSTM; GRU; cell state; gates
pitfalls: Gate diagrams should distinguish LSTM and GRU equations.
A hidden state is a compressed learned representation, not a lossless transcript.

concepts.title: Policy and environment loop
concepts.meaning: Improves a policy through repeated state, action, outcome, and reward feedback.
concepts.brief: Show a state or observation entering a policy, an action changing the environment, and the next observation and reward returning to the learner. Keep episodic return separate from one-step reward; include a replayable trajectory for the LLM case.
pitfalls: A reward function is a training signal, not a complete specification of human value.
Observed reward may arrive later than the action that produced it.

concepts.title: Retrieval fusion and reranking
concepts.meaning: Combines candidate lists from complementary retrieval methods, then spends more compute on a shortlist.
concepts.brief: Route one query through sparse lexical and dense vector lanes, merge ranked lists with a labeled fusion step, rerank a small candidate set with a joint query-document scorer, and surface evidence spans.
concepts.aliases: hybrid retrieval; reciprocal-rank fusion; cross-encoder reranking
pitfalls: Candidate retrieval locates evidence; it does not grant permission or prove answer support.
Keep shortlist size and expensive scoring boundary visible.

concepts.title: Reward-model exploitation loop
concepts.meaning: Shows how optimizing a proxy reward can amplify behaviors that score well while missing the intended human objective.
concepts.brief: Place a target-quality axis beside proxy reward; move a policy update through examples that exploit verbosity, sycophancy, or format shortcuts, and compare proxy gains with fresh human evaluation.
concepts.aliases: Goodhart effects; reward hacking; proxy overoptimization
pitfalls: The model can exploit evaluator correlations without an explicit intention to deceive.
Use concrete failure examples and report the evaluation distribution.

concepts.title: Roofline performance model
concepts.meaning: Bounds kernel throughput by peak compute and memory bandwidth at a given arithmetic intensity.
concepts.brief: Plot arithmetic intensity on a log x-axis and attainable performance on y; draw bandwidth slope, compute ceiling, ridge point, and one labeled kernel moving across the boundary.
concepts.aliases: roofline; bandwidth-bound; compute-bound; ridge point
pitfalls: The roofline is a bound under stated hardware and measurement assumptions.
Occupancy, launch overhead, cache behavior, and synchronization can lower measured performance further.

concepts.title: Sampling distributions and bootstrap
concepts.meaning: Uses repeated samples to show how an estimator varies under finite data and dependence assumptions.
concepts.brief: Draw a population and sample, then repeatedly resample rows with replacement to form an empirical distribution for a statistic; show paired resampling and effective sample size where relevant.
concepts.aliases: bootstrap; sampling variability; Monte Carlo; effective sample size
pitfalls: Bootstrap validity depends on the sampling unit and dependence structure.
A narrow interval cannot repair biased or unrepresentative data.

concepts.title: Softmax distribution
concepts.meaning: Turns a row of raw scores into normalized probability mass over competing choices.
concepts.brief: Place logits as signed bars, subtract the maximum, exponentiate, and normalize into a second probability row. Let temperature change how concentrated the mass becomes; keep the target token and cumulative top-p cutoff as optional overlays.
concepts.aliases: softmax; categorical probabilities; normalized logits
pitfalls: Probability mass alone does not establish empirical calibration.
Keep stable max-shift arithmetic visible when teaching overflow.

concepts.title: Sparse autoencoder feature view
concepts.meaning: Maps activations into a wider sparse feature space and reconstructs the original activation.
concepts.brief: Show a transformer activation vector entering an overcomplete encoder, a small set of active feature bars, and decoder contributions reconstructing the original vector; optionally visualize feature overlap in a toy 2D model.
concepts.aliases: SAE; feature dictionary; superposition; sparse code
pitfalls: Learned features are hypotheses that require validation, not automatically faithful human concepts.
Show reconstruction error and sparsity pressure together.

concepts.title: Synthetic data admission loop
concepts.meaning: Generates candidate training examples and filters them against quality, execution, safety, and diversity checks.
concepts.brief: Compose seed examples, generator, deterministic verifier, calibrated judge/human review, deduplication, and admitted dataset; show rejected rows with reasons and preserve source lineage.
concepts.aliases: synthetic data; verifier; admission filters; data flywheel
pitfalls: Generated volume does not establish capability gain.
Keep contamination, recursive model collapse, and lineage risks visible.

concepts.title: Task-vector model merging
concepts.meaning: Represents a fine-tune as a parameter difference from a shared base and combines such deltas.
concepts.brief: Place a base checkpoint as an origin, draw task vectors from it, and show weighted addition, subtraction, sign conflict, and a validation gate for a merged candidate.
concepts.aliases: task arithmetic; model soup; TIES; DARE; SLERP
pitfalls: Weight coordinates must be compatible; matching tensor shapes alone does not ensure semantic alignment.
A merged model requires fresh evaluation.

concepts.title: Teacher-student distillation
concepts.meaning: Trains a smaller student to match information from a larger teacher through soft targets, features, or generated responses.
concepts.brief: Align teacher and student token distributions at a shared temperature; show KL loss on soft logits, optional feature matching, and response-data transfer when vocabularies do not align.
concepts.aliases: knowledge distillation; soft labels; teacher/student; temperature
pitfalls: Teacher confidence may encode errors and biases.
Token-level logit matching requires compatible vocabularies and alignment.

concepts.title: Temporal feature availability
concepts.meaning: Checks that each training/evaluation feature was available at the prediction decision time.
concepts.brief: Place prediction time, feature event time, ingestion/availability time, and label-maturity time on one entity timeline; shade only values eligible for the row and compare with a leaking future join.
concepts.aliases: point-in-time join; temporal leakage; as-of join
pitfalls: Event timestamps alone do not prove a value was known to the system then.
Availability is row- and entity-specific.

concepts.title: Classification threshold sweep
concepts.meaning: Shows how a decision threshold changes classifications and precision/recall trade-offs.
concepts.brief: Sort scored examples along one axis and drag a threshold; update TP/FP/FN/TN, precision, recall, and ROC or precision-recall point in sync.
concepts.aliases: decision threshold; ROC; precision-recall curve
pitfalls: Threshold choice depends on costs, prevalence, and operating policy.
An ROC curve can look strong under severe class imbalance.

concepts.title: Subword tokenization algorithms
concepts.meaning: Segments text into token IDs under a fixed vocabulary and tokenizer-specific rules.
concepts.brief: Put the same Unicode string through parallel BPE, WordPiece, and SentencePiece lanes. Reveal pair-frequency merges, greedy longest-match pieces, and Unigram alternative segmentations with IDs and detokenization.
concepts.aliases: BPE; WordPiece; SentencePiece; Unigram LM; subword segmentation
pitfalls: Token boundaries are model-specific and part of the checkpoint contract.
Show Unicode bytes/normalization when relevant; do not imply word-like boundaries always hold.

concepts.title: Training step state machine
concepts.meaning: Orders gradient reset, forward computation, loss evaluation, backward propagation, and optimizer update.
concepts.brief: Build a loop state machine with tensors, gradients, optimizer moments, and counters as persistent state; show accumulation steps joining before a single optimizer update and checkpoint boundary.
concepts.aliases: forward/backward/update loop; gradient accumulation; checkpoint boundary
pitfalls: Gradient accumulation sums or averages gradients according to the trainer contract.
A completed microbatch is not necessarily an optimizer update.

concepts.title: Variational autoencoder path
concepts.meaning: Encodes an input as a latent distribution, samples a code, and trains a decoder under reconstruction and prior-matching terms.
concepts.brief: Move a small image through encoder outputs μ and σ, sample with z=μ+σϵ, decode a reconstruction, and plot prior/posterior latent points with reconstruction and KL terms.
concepts.aliases: VAE; ELBO; reparameterization trick; latent code
pitfalls: A latent point is a learned code; coordinates need not have human-interpretable meaning.
The KL term encourages prior matching but can contribute to posterior collapse.
